You have a MSD81 and the N53 engine. This engine is not available in the US and it's not supported by bimmerlabs. There is an RSA Delete for the MSD81 because it's the same DME for the N54. BUT N53 and N54 use different ROM versions. N54 uses IJE0S (mainly) and N53 uses IHF0S!

There is a solution to get the 330i file onto your 325i. The steps are:

1. Flash the correct 330i ZB# with WinKFP (comfort mode works fine)
2. Read it with kess.
3. Locate the power class byte and change it.
4. Flash it back with kess.
5. Have fun.

You will need to change your manifold for the 3-stage manifold from the 330i otherwise it will throw errors because of the missing DISA actuators. It is possible to deactivate the DISA error if you know the location in the .bin file.

Some earlier N53's < 03/2008 use the MSD80 but they also use a different ROM version.

Here are some comparison charts with torque and power numbers:

https://drive.google.com/drive/folde...wXBr4vq8xsm40_

Both are converted from 325i to 330i, one without the 3-stage manifold, one with 3-stage manifold. These are calculated values from the DME without drivetrain loss. The real values are lower but you can see a good difference with and without 3-stage manifold. The RPM range is not ideal but you can see the difference in maximum values. Unfortunately I don't have values from a stock 325i.

The N53 engines usually have less power than BMW claims. Dynos are generally useless if you don't do a dyno run before the conversion. Important is that you always use RON98 fuel or better for full power. With RON95 the DME loweres the ignition timing and you have less power.

I did multiple cars with this method and it works just fine.

#2348 (Page 107)Joluga123New Member
02-27-2022, 11:06 AM
BMW Z4SocalJun 2019
Update,

After checking everywhere for possible causes, I found not much info regarding the "2DE3 message instrument panel missing", my instrumental panel is working fine, I have no issues whatsoever, I do feel the difference in power, DISA and 3 stage intake is working. I decided to remove the manifold I put the stock back.
Then I found that the cable from the power box to the knock sensors (ping sensors) was damaged by rodents. It did not have the corrugated plastic shield (I realized this after looking up the replacement part), just the cable itself.

I removed the cable and it was in fact broken. where the arrow is pointing at. See picture #1,
Wires were exposed, I'm not even sure if these sensors retain any charge, but when I took the picture I even saw a small spark.

I ordered the cables, hopefully, this resolves my issue, and no permanent damage was done to my DME.

I will report when I put everything back.

This is a bit inconclusive, but I came up with an idea of simply using stock 330i tune from bimmerlabs.

I am pretty sure MSV80 330i did not exist in the US, being replaced by 328i and 335i. I managed to find a 2010 E92 330i (258hp) for sale in my region, EU spec, and used its vin in bimmerlabs, downloaded the stock tune (8608462) for that car and flashed it.

Guess what? DMTL and 2FA3 code went away and car runs even better than the 328i to 330i tune (Which I had to change the powerclass byte myself otherwise the car would go into limp mode).

In short, bimmerlabs US 328i VIN RSA delete + EU 330i stock tune = working EU 325i to 330i engine swapped car.

And another added-bonus, I added VO $199 (no catalytic converter and leaded fuel, according to forum posts) in NCS Expert and coded DME, my hollowed out factory headers no longer throw code, so I guess it's success for my poor man's straight pipes.

(P.S.1: I am going to run the car for a while and see if it works as 330i, but I am probably eventually going to get a custom tune for $450 at 22RPD and actual headers, which again is kind of a shame bimmerlabs isn't "commercially" active and there isn't much community tuning/map editing out there)

(P.S.2: I flashed everything with a generic green PCB cable that I got in 2017, RSA delete took ~22 minutes and 0da ~1 minute, have a bimmergeeks cable on order but got impatient.)

In summary of my research and trials so far, I believe:

bimmerlabs 328i to 330i tune is essentially 330i map + powerclass change (powerclass set to 1 but DME ignores it). This requires RSA delete as the files are altered.

For someone like me swapping N52B30 into 325i, which is already powerclass 2, I believe I could have simply flashed stock 330i 0da and it would work without RSA delete, since it's original BMW file.





AKA: if you are doing 28i to 30i, I suggest you could try flashing a stock 30i tune (that's same region as yours) but you would have to change the powerclass byte, cheerio had some info on this and I simply use the address they found for the E90 (0x219 if i remember correctly). Otherwise you could try using their script to find the byte location and change it yourself.

Try setting lc_var_sof_swi to 01 (0x423FF in MI20S; I can find it in other program versions if you're on something else)

CONF_SOF_SWI is a RAM address, but the above should be the constant that controls it.

You will need to correct or disable the MO3 checksums to change that value.

Quote:

A few things I'm not clear on, are the process for going back to stock. I couldn't find much info on this. Like where in INPA are the values you need to look for, which of the 3 stock files do you flash and in what order?
Lucky I didn't have to revert back to stock, but I did some preparation... just in case!

I'm not sure of the steps off the top of my head, but it'd be roughly -->
Plug laptop into your car
Position2
Open up INPA:
Should have 2x Black Dots
<Select Car Model> (See https://www.e90post.com/forums/showp...05&postcount=4)
<Select your engine>
Then go to Identification and then User Information

I'm no expert, but this should provide your existing:
--> Part Number = aka HW# *.0pa (from Identification)
--> Assembly = aka ZB# (from User Info)
--> Calibration dataset = aka *.0da (from User Info)

"Calibration dataset" is always "Assembly"-1 OR "*0da" is always "ZB#" -1


Then as per my writeup, you can then just open up your engine data file in your Datens location using Notepad:
SP-Daten\E89\data\MSV80\MSV80.dat and confirm the rows that have the Assembly (ZB#) and Calibration dataset (*.0da) that matches your HW (*.0pa)

Once you've got that, you should be able to just use one of the Stock batch files from Bimmerlabs... If not, edit one and copy across the corresponding file(s) (from your datens).
*** NOTE - You can edit the Bimmerlabs Stock files (*.CTL and *.BAT) using notepad to see which files are being referenced (*.PRG, *.IPO, *0pa and *.0da)
I think it's just 1x *.0pa, followed by the 1x *.0da
Interesting to note: after successfully running the Bimmerlabs 125 to 130 tune, INPA reports that my HW changed from 7594483 to 7602220

Due to the stark similarities between both MSV70 and MSD80 DME's, my guess is that ip_iga_min_n_maf_puc_opm_1 and 2 are the trailing throttle fuel cut (PUC) ignition maps.

I personally use a very very similar map on my N54 and it works wonders if someone wants to tweak their burble to their liking. I can't verify it for anyone as my friends car never starts after flashing the RSA Delete and tune file afterwards.

ip_mff_cor_opm_1_1 (1_2, 2_1 and 2_2) are the fuel scalar maps for those running extensive mods and may or may not be useful.

For anyone that wants less nannies in the software, I would disable DROF, lc_tq_iga_inh, lc_tq_lim_inh (general), lc_tq_lim_inh_fast, lc_tq_lim_inh_slow. Setting those toggles to 1 should disable it.

I would also recommend simulating the 1M throttle maps by changing the torque request maps and copying the 1M values and breakpoints and reducing the throttle correction (ip_fac_pv_bas_cor_transmission) to 0 on MT (reduce numbers by half for a good starting point on automatic cars as they get real twitchy at 0)

I can't provide any guarantees as the only MSV70 I have access to doesn't even start up after BimmerLabs batch flashing. I have tested out all of these maps on my MSD80 though.

#2438 (Page 111)firesnatchPrivate
04-10-2025, 10:01 AM
2008 328i 6MTAurora, ILApr 2011
I asked ChatGPT and it said to try the following. I take no responsibility if this is wrong or destroys your car

🔧 Step-by-Step: Update Power Class Without CAS
- Launch NCS Expert
Use the "Expertmode" profile.
- Read the FA (Vehicle Order)
Select chassis: E85
Select ECU: choose AKMB
Press F2 (FA/VO) → then F1 (Enter VIN) → enter your VIN
Press F6 (Back)
- Change FA/VO Power Class
Press F4 (Process ECU) → select AKMB
Press F5 (Change ZCS/FA)
Add or update 6BMOT with the correct power class code (e.g., N46, M54, etc.)
Then press F6 (Back) to return.
- Write the Updated FA to Modules
Press F6 (Back) again
Press F5 (Change ZCS/FA) again if needed
Then choose AKMB, and then ALSZ to write the new FA to both modules.
NCS Expert should confirm the new FA has been written.

0x2191 is for MSV80 and I messed it up in my note

4D50 is the address for MSV70, and according to your ZB num yours is 00


I've modified 7581342 to 00 correctly this time

Open the PDF file with editor and safe as .0pa file again (couldn't upload zip file because of size restriction).

Furthermore, let's talk about the N53B30UL/OL power class.

UL = Untere Leistung = 00
OL = Obere Leistung = 02

I compared 330i and 325i in a hex editor and found 4 possible power class adresses, but only one makes sense: 0x3a14

EUDM E92 325i 2006ItalyFeb 2022
i used this with some success to tune my own car.

v11_XDF_MSV80_0049QK0MI20S.zip

Built it using an MSV70 XDF and relative bin, and trying to find exact matches for msv80 bin data (endian swap and all), and some euristics...

I was helped by chatGPT, built me some (many) python scripts and something i did by eye

Not nearly complete, but all the good stuff is there:

- lambda full load and part load
- cat heating routines
- idle control
- rev limiters
- ignition logic
- vanos targets
- disa

and a lot of other stuff

DISCLAIMER: i used this and tuned my car with success, but i do not guarantee you will too. i used a sw tool for flashing, called MSV80Flasher, about 30 dollars or such. It does RSA delete and checksums, works 9 out of 10 times but when bricked i always was able to repair using same tool and reflash

PS: if someone wants to take it and add some more stuff (objective would be to map every MSV70 parameter in this MSV80 xdf if possible) - feel free to do it but SHARE IT

at the moment it looks like ball was dropped on MSV80 mapping

#2500 (Page 114)JrosPrivate First Class
03-25-2026, 02:22 PM
EUDM E92 325i 2006ItalyFeb 2022
some stuff that i discovered, to be taken with a grain of salt

- milvs tuning escapes me - there is no need to alter any model from what i see, and changing targets for the eccentric shaft gains nothing. I never seen any indicator that the car isn't managing by itself the slightly more airmass

- car runs pig rich over 6k in stock rom

- car doesn't like a lot of ignition advance around 6k, tried to play a bit with the logic and by my timed logs there was no difference between mean 23° adv and mean 26° adv in the 4.5k to 7k band, so kept stock ignition

- car likes to pull timing for no reason, may be mine does: resolved lowering knock preamp for some cells

- going richer than 0.92 - 0.90 is useless

- best gain to get is removing the soft limiter logic / retuning it

- played with vanos targets, only gain I had (almost noise, not 10 hp) was retarding exhaust with a ramp that touches -115 at 7k

- no need to touch the torque model if NA, i see no intervention even if actual tq from model goes somewhat over commanded, no closure of valvetronic or throttle, no ign pull

these considerations are from tuning an euro 330i base software, the famous "factory mafless" one
